issue.title: Staged-monitor owner index entries outlive dismissed held members
issue.description:
Listed as an out-of-scope follow-up in epic sase-1ux's plan
(plan:202611/failed_clan_visibility.md, "Owner-index leaks"); filed by the sase-1ux land
agent after re-verifying on athena.

Root cause (from source): `cleanup_staged_monitor(held=True)` in
`src/sase/monitor/start_stage_cleanup.py` deliberately keeps the staged-owner index
(`~/.sase/staged-monitor-owners/<monitor_id>.json`) so `sase agent readopt` can find the
held member (custody rule from sase-1rg.8, commit 956310b7ad). The only deletions are
`clear_staged_owner_index` on successful adoption (`start_launch.py`,
`_start_stage_adopt_proc.py`) and on non-held discard. When a held member is later
dismissed or its artifact dir is removed, nothing clears its owner-index entry.

Evidence on athena, 2026-11-22: 6 entries exist; 4 point at member artifact dirs that no
longer exist (`0yn961767pq8`, `4mbt06rp80w2`, `k0jynj8q7ygf`, `xsf0de5y1fjf`, the last
being incident member `tailnet-1e.6.1.8--mon-0`). The other 2 (`sase-1r2.6--mon-2`,
`1dt--mon`) are live held stages and must stay.

Fix shape: clear the owner index when a held member is dismissed or purged, and/or have
housekeeping sweep entries whose `artifacts_dir` is gone. Keep the readopt custody rule:
never delete the entry for a held member that still exists.

task_type_fields.impact: Unbounded small-file leak in ~/.sase and stale readopt lookups that point at members that no longer exist.
task_type_fields.repro: Stage a monitor, let the starter fail so cleanup_staged_monitor(held=True) runs, then dismiss or delete the held member's artifact dir. ~/.sase/staged-monitor-owners/<monitor_id>.json remains forever, pointing at a missing artifacts_dir.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1ux's plan listed owner-index leaks as out of scope; the land agent confirmed four orphaned entries on athena and the missing cleanup path in source.

payload.description: Active phase settling orphaned/held staged monitors; must keep the owner-index custody rule this fix touches
